This semi-real application evaluates silicate prediction with partially observed
oxygen inputs. Measured records are retained as references; ordinal records and
nested measurement masks are constructed on a fixed, class-balanced cohort.

## 1. Computation settings

- **Workflow:** `ocean-eivGP.R` and `ocean-competitors.R` each fit and analyze their method group with one shared core budget; `ocean-report.R` assembles this report from saved results. Use `--reuse-only=true` on the method scripts to prohibit fitting.
- **Action:** `report` reads saved fits; `plan` displays the proposed analysis without fitting.
- **Dataset:** `ocean200`, `ocean500` or `ocean1000`; prepare the 1000-profile folds once using `data/ocean_silicate/prepare_folds.R`.
- **Selection:** `folds`, `cells` and `modules` select tasks without changing seeds or numerical settings.
- **Results:** default to the latest run under `<repository>/results/<dataset>/` (pilot/quick roots append the profile); set `output_dir` to select a specific saved run.
- **Distributed runs:** use separate result roots and merge compatible tasks through `import_dirs`.

Runnable examples are in `README_ocean.md`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,cache=FALSE,error=FALSE)
Sys.setenv(OMP_NUM_THREADS="1",OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS="1",MKL_NUM_THREADS="1",VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS="1")
if(!params$action %in% c("report","plan"))
  stop("Run ocean-eivGP.R and ocean-competitors.R, then ocean-report.R; render this Rmd with action='report'.")
if(any(nzchar(as.character(unlist(params$import_dirs)))))
  stop("Import results with ocean.R --import-dirs=... before rendering the report.")
dataset<-match.arg(params$dataset,c("ocean200","ocean500","ocean1000"))
input <- knitr::current_input(dir=TRUE)
repository_dir <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(input),"../.."),mustWork=TRUE)
source(file.path(dirname(input),"ocean.R"),local=TRUE)
ocean_load_api(repository_dir,environment())
prediction_labels <- ocean_prediction_labels()
settings <- ocean_settings(profile=params$profile,action=params$action,folds=params$folds,
  cells=params$cells,modules=params$modules,task_ids=params$task_ids,cores=params$cores,run_id=params$run_id)
data_dir <- ocean_dataset_dir(repository_dir,dataset,params$data_dir)
output_dir <- ocean_output_dir(repository_dir,dataset,settings$profile,params$output_dir)
identity_path <- ocean_path(output_dir,"workflow_identity.rds")
if(file.exists(identity_path)) {
  saved_numerics <- readRDS(identity_path)$numerics
  for(key in c("chains","iter","burn"))settings[[key]] <- saved_numerics[[key]]
}
if(settings$action=="report" && !dir.exists(output_dir))
  stop("Saved results not found: ",output_dir,". Run the method scripts first, or specify the existing output_dir.")
diagnostics_dir <- if(nzchar(params$diagnostics_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$diagnostics_dir,repository_dir) else ocean_path(output_dir,"diagnostics")
import_dirs <- as.character(unlist(params$import_dirs)); import_dirs <- import_dirs[nzchar(import_dirs)]
import_dirs <- ocean_resolve_path(import_dirs,repository_dir)
cc_output_dir <- if(nzchar(params$cc_output_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$cc_output_dir,repository_dir) else output_dir
inputs <- ocean_prepare_inputs(data_dir)
selected <- ocean_select_tasks(settings)
```

```{r selected-work, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("Selected work: **%d base tasks** and **%d conditional continuation candidates**.\n\n",
  sum(selected$module!="continuation"),sum(selected$module=="continuation")))
```

```{r computation-summary, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
  settings$chains,settings$iter,settings$burn))
```

## 2. Data and observation design

### Notation

| Symbol | Application variable |
|---|---|
| \(y\) | Silicate response |
| \(u\) | Continuous oxygen input |
| \(c\) | Ordinal oxygen record: \([0,50),[50,100),[100,150),[150,180)\) |
| \(x\) | Salinity and natural-log pressure |

Concentrations are in micromol/kg. In test tables, **\((x,c)\)** denotes inputs
without observed \(u\); **\((x,u)\)** denotes inputs with observed \(u\).

### Data-use protocols

The suffixes describe how training records and test inputs are used. Native
comparators retain \(c\) as a categorical input when \(u\) is observed.

```{r protocol-definitions, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat(ocean_prediction_protocols(prediction_labels),"\n\n")
```

Test-input percentages are computed from the observation masks; sample counts
are reported separately in the design and results tables.

### Cohort construction

- **Source:** GLODAPv2.2023 Pacific merged and adjusted product; 10--50 degrees N, 140--240 degrees E.
- **Quality filters:** finite temperature/salinity, positive oxygen, and oxygen/silicate/nitrate flags equal to 2. Nitrate is not a predictor.
- **Analysis domain:** pressure 300--1500 dbar and \(0<u<180\).
- **Sampling unit:** one bottle per cruise--station profile. Selection balances the four \(c\) levels, within-level oxygen quartiles and log-pressure halves.

The class boundaries specify an imposed recording rule, not oceanographic regimes.
The cohort followed exploratory screening; frozen folds subsequently balanced
input strata and salinity without using responses.

```{r cohort-range, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("The selected cohort contains **%d profiles from %d cruises**, with actual ranges %.3f--%.3f degrees N, %.2f--%.2f degrees E and %.1f--%.1f dbar.\n\n",
  nrow(inputs$cohort),length(unique(inputs$cohort$G2cruise)),
  min(inputs$cohort$G2latitude),max(inputs$cohort$G2latitude),
  min(inputs$cohort$G2longitude),max(inputs$cohort$G2longitude),
  min(inputs$cohort$G2pressure),max(inputs$cohort$G2pressure)))
```

### Training and test information

- **Per fold:** `r inputs$design$n_train` training and `r inputs$design$n_test` test profiles, with `r inputs$design$n_train/4`/`r inputs$design$n_test/4` per \(c\) level.
- **Training:** \((x,c,y)\) observed for all `r inputs$design$n_train` profiles. O0/O20/O50 additionally reveal \(u\) for `r paste(inputs$design$train_exact,collapse="/")` profiles; nested subsets retain cut-side anchors.
- **Testing:** either \((x,c)\) for all profiles, or \((x,u)\) for `r paste(inputs$design$test_exact[-1],collapse="/")` profiles and \((x,c)\) for the remainder. Test masks are nested, class-balanced up to integer rounding, and identical across methods.
- **Separation:** test \(y\) is excluded from fitting/tuning. Transformations use training data; \(u\) scaling uses training calibration measurements. Hidden reference \(u\) is used only for design, evaluation and offline plots.

```{r observation-information, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
design_review <- ocean_design_review(inputs)
cat(ocean_table_html(design_review$design,"Observed information per fold",
  "All training y observed; all test y withheld. The partial-u condition is evaluated at O20/O50 only. Test masks use seed 202609260 + fold."))
```

### EIV-GP targets and comparator scope

The EIV-GP hierarchy defines the targets below; comparators share only the
applicable response targets.

\[
m_{f,\psi}(x,c)=\int f(x,u)Q_\psi(du\mid x,c).
\]

| Target | Evaluation and comparator scope |
|---|---|
| **Held-out \(y\) prediction** | All methods are scored on matched profiles and available inputs. EIV-GP uses \(p(y^*\mid x^*,c^*,D)\) or \(p(y^*\mid x^*,u^*,D)\); baselines use native predictors. |
| **Observable mean \(m(x,c)\)** | EIV-GP integrates its conditional \(u\) law; original \((x,c)\) baselines estimate the recorded-input mean directly. True \(m\) is unavailable. |
| **Calibrated surface \(f(x,u)\)** | Displayed for EIV-GP. CC comparators define their own response functions of \((x,u,c)\); these are not the same EIV hierarchy. True \(f\) is unavailable. |
| **Training-input posterior \(p(u_i\mid D)\)** | EIV-GP only; uses training \(y_i\) and is evaluated against masked reference \(u_i\). Baselines provide no individual physical-input posterior. |

Conclusions concern this selected cohort and imposed observation design. Profiles
are disjoint across training/test sets, but cruises can overlap; new-cruise or
regional transfer, natural missingness and causal effects are not established.

### Observed data

```{r data-design}
cohort <- inputs$cohort
levels(cohort$oxygen_class) <- c("<50","50-100","100-150","150-180")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(cohort$oxygen_class)),
  col.names=c("Oxygen class (micromol/kg)","Observations"))
```

```{r exploratory-plots, eval=settings$action!="plan", fig.width=10, fig.height=3.8}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
ocean_cohort_plot(inputs$cohort)
```

## 3. Model fitting and numerical assessment

The following chunk reads saved fits, predictions and imputations. Model fitting
and analysis are combined in the two method scripts. Explicit continuation remains available through `ocean.R --action=continue`; the report script never extends chains.

```{r saved-results, class.source="fold-show", results="hide"}
snapshot<-get0(".ocean_precomputed_analysis",inherits=TRUE)
if(!is.null(snapshot)) {
  stopifnot(identical(snapshot$output_dir,normalizePath(output_dir)),
    identical(snapshot$data_dir,normalizePath(data_dir)),identical(snapshot$profile,settings$profile),
    identical(snapshot$folds,settings$folds),identical(snapshot$cells,settings$cells))
  analysis<-snapshot$analysis
} else {
analysis <- ocean_analysis(
  repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, settings,
  cc_output_dir=cc_output_dir, diagnostics_dir=diagnostics_dir,
  representative_fold=params$representative_fold
)
}
```

- **EIV-GP:** a joint response/input model with deterministic ordinal thresholds. The working input population is standard Gaussian and independent of \(x\).
- **Native comparators:** UC-GP, LVGP and EzGP use all training \((x,c,y)\) records for `r prediction_labels[["xc"]]`, or only complete \((x,u,c,y)\) records for `r prediction_labels[["cc"]]`. Complete-case continuous inputs are standardized using that training subset.
- **Test scope:** complete-case methods and EIV-GP are compared on the same observed-\(u\) test subset. The mixed-input EIV rule additionally predicts the entire test set. No missing test \(u\) is filled for the complete-case methods.
- **Result roots:** `output_dir` supplies EIV/recorded-input fits; `cc_output_dir` supplies independently verified CC tasks. 

```{r fitting-overview, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
ocean_fit_overview(analysis, output_dir)
```

```{r diagnostics-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
diagnostics <- analysis$diagnostics
surfaces <- analysis$surfaces
diagnostic_run <- analysis$diagnostic_run
```

```{r paper-export-status, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(analysis$paper_assets)) {
  cat("**Paper export status:** ",analysis$paper_assets$status,"\n\n",sep="")
  print(knitr::kable(analysis$paper_assets$manifest[,c("label","file","status")]))
  cat("\n\nSee reports/paper/method_status.csv for unavailable comparisons. Completion is separate from convergence.\n")
}
```

```{r surfaces-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
  all(vapply(1:5,function(f) file.exists(ocean_path(output_dir,"full5_class4",sprintf("fold%02d",f),"baseline_package_outputs.rds")),logical(1))))
  surfaces <- ocean_surface_report(output_dir,data_dir,diagnostics_dir,representative_fold=params$representative_fold)
```

```{r saved-review-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
saved_review <- if(!is.null(analysis$paper_assets$review)) analysis$paper_assets$review else ocean_refinement_review(output_dir,inputs,diagnostics)
```

### Scientific-target traceplots

```{r scientific-target-traces, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=7.1, fig.height=6.5}
if(!is.null(analysis$paper_assets$review$targets)) {
  targets <- analysis$paper_assets$review$targets
  print(ocean_target_trace_plot(targets$traces))
  cat("Target-specific checks complement the raw-coordinate screen. Function diagnostics use 256 evaluated states per chain; oxygen diagnostics use full retained chains. Conditional-mean traces do not assess all posterior uncertainty or tail precision.\n\n")
  cat(ocean_table_html(targets$summary,"Scientific-target R-hat, ESS and Monte Carlo precision"))
}
```

<details>
<summary>Supplementary: computation and posterior approximation</summary>

- **Package calls:** the `run_eiv()` routine created by `ocean_initial_functions()` in the Ocean section of `eivGP/R/helpers.R` calls `fit_eivgp()`, `predict_eivgp()` and `impute_eivgp()`; selected continuations call `continue_eivgp()`.
- **Native baselines:** the pinned `run_published_mixedgp_competitors()` adapter calls kergp, LVGP and EzGP fitting/prediction routines. CC `package_status.csv` retains optimizer status and warnings. A finite prediction can be returned with a flagged optimizer code; task completion alone does not establish optimizer convergence.
- **Explicit continuation:** `ocean.R --action=continue` adds one extra round with `r paste(format(ocean_continuation_lengths(output_dir,settings$profile),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE),collapse=" / ")` iterations per chain (saved task budgets; configurable with `--continuation-iter`) if initial maximum finite Rhat exceeds 1.01, minimum finite bulk ESS is below 400, or finite values are unavailable; `u_block_size=8`.
- **Review:** finite diagnostics, tail ESS and undefined values are reported separately. Passing the screen does not establish model adequacy, identification or precision of every functional.

```{r saved-chain-review, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=10, fig.height=7.5}
if(!is.null(saved_review)) {
  numerical <- diagnostics$provenance$settings
  cat(sprintf("**Function calculations:** %d posterior states per chain; %d latent integration nodes for m(x,c); %d/%d GP draws per state for m/f intervals.\n\n",
    numerical$mean_states_per_chain,numerical$n_latent,numerical$mean_gp_draws,numerical$surface_gp_draws))
  d<-saved_review$mcmc
  d$max_finite_Rhat<-sprintf("%.4f",d$max_finite_Rhat)
  d$min_finite_bulk_ESS<-round(d$min_finite_bulk_ESS); d$min_finite_tail_ESS<-round(d$min_finite_tail_ESS)
  cat(ocean_table_html(d,"Final-fit numerical screen",
    "Finite screen uses Rhat <= 1.01 and bulk ESS >= 400. Tail ESS and counts of undefined diagnostics are displayed, without retroactively changing the continuation rule."))
  ex<-saved_review$exceptions
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**%d parameter-by-fit exceptions** are reviewed separately. Constant indicators include unvisited dictionary states; exploration of rare states is not established. Per-chain assessments are exported in diagnostics/refinement/exceptions.csv.\n\n",nrow(ex)))
  print(saved_review$trace)
  q<-saved_review$precision
  d<-data.frame(Quantity=q$parameter,"Posterior mean"=sprintf("%.3f",q$mean),
    "Posterior SD"=sprintf("%.3f",q$posterior_sd),"MCSE of mean"=sprintf("%.4f",q$mcse),check.names=FALSE)
  cat(ocean_table_html(d,"Focused Monte Carlo precision on complete saved chains",
    sprintf("Same fit and six quantities as the trace plot: fold %d/%s. MCSE uses complete chains and measures precision of posterior means. At O0, u and cutpoints use working-model units. Individual-interval and full prediction/function precision remain unassessed.",saved_review$selected$fold,saved_review$selected$cell)))
} else cat("Saved-chain checks are pending complete final fits.\n")
```

## 4. Response prediction

For EIV-GP, prediction means average \(m(x,c)\) for \((x,c)\) inputs and
\(f(x,u)\) for \((x,u)\) inputs. The tables score held-out \(y\), not true
\(m/f\) recovery.

- **RMSE:** point prediction error; **CRPS:** predictive-distribution loss (lower is better).
- **Coverage/width:** 95% response intervals. EIV-GP includes response noise, posterior uncertainty and unresolved \(u\); native baselines include fitted noise/nugget without integrating missing physical \(u\).
- **Normalization:** \(s_Y\) is the frozen cohort response SD, used only to scale reported scores/widths.
Method suffixes follow the data-use protocols defined in Section 2. For EIV-GP,
`r prediction_labels[["xc"]]` uses \(m(x,c)\); `r prediction_labels[["mixed"]]` routes
between \(m(x,c)\) and \(f(x,u)\) according to observed test information.

```{r prediction-table, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cc_review <- analysis$cc_review
cc_review$SD_Y <- inputs$response_sd
ocean_show_cc_predictions(cc_review,section="full")
```

### Complete-case comparison

Each CC comparator is fitted only to training profiles with observed \(u\), using
continuous \((x,u)\), categorical \(c\) and response \(y\). Training profiles without
measured \(u\) are omitted. EIV-GP retains all training profiles.

Within each calibration condition, all methods are evaluated on the same test
profiles with observed \(u\). EIV-GP(`r prediction_labels[["mixed"]]`) uses its \(f(x,u)\) route on this subset.
These subset scores have a different evaluation population from the preceding
all-profile table.

```{r complete-case-table, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
ocean_show_cc_predictions(cc_review,section="cc")
```

```{r prediction-evidence-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
eiv_report <- analysis$prediction
eiv_report$fold_metrics <- eiv_report$fold_metrics[eiv_report$fold_metrics$variant=="EIV" & eiv_report$fold_metrics$fold %in% settings$folds,]
evidence <- ocean_prediction_evidence(output_dir,inputs,eiv_report,
  profile=settings$profile,dest=ocean_path(output_dir,"prediction_report","cc_revision","eiv_evidence"))
if(!is.null(evidence))evidence$expected_folds <- settings$folds
```

```{r cc-pooled-rmse, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
ocean_show_cc_pooled(cc_review)
```

</details>

### EIV-GP: `r prediction_labels[["xc"]]` versus `r prediction_labels[["mixed"]]` on matched test profiles

For the **same observed-\(u\) profiles and trained fit**, compare EIV-GP(`r prediction_labels[["xc"]]`) with EIV-GP(`r prediction_labels[["mixed"]]`). The latter uses its \(f(x,u)\) route on these profiles. Training and evaluation profiles remain fixed.

```{r mixed-subgroups, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(evidence) && nrow(evidence$information)) {
  d <- ocean_evidence_table(evidence,"information",eiv_only=TRUE,labels=prediction_labels)
  d <- ocean_table_columns(d,setdiff(names(d),c("Method","Mean delta SE","Mean |prediction change|")))
  cat(ocean_table_html(d,sprintf("EIV-GP: paired %s-%s comparison",prediction_labels[["xc"]],prediction_labels[["mixed"]]),
    "Same profiles and trained fit. Bold marks the smaller paired RMSE; negative delta CRPS favors measured u. Descriptive comparison only."))
}
```

<details>
<summary>Supplementary: EIV-GP(`r prediction_labels[["xc"]]`/`r prediction_labels[["mixed"]]`) prediction summaries</summary>

```{r prediction-evidence-details, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(evidence))for(type in c("subgroups","pooled")) {
  d <- ocean_evidence_table(evidence,type,labels=prediction_labels)
  if(nrow(d))cat(ocean_table_html(d,if(type=="subgroups")sprintf("EIV-GP(%s): test-input subset scores",prediction_labels[["mixed"]]) else sprintf("EIV-GP(%s/%s): pooled held-out scores",prediction_labels[["xc"]],prediction_labels[["mixed"]]),
    "Pooled RMSE takes the square root after pooling squared errors. Main tables average fold RMSEs. Evaluation subsets contain different profiles; compare the named protocols on matched profiles in the paired table."),"\n\n")
}
```

Fold SD describes variation across overlapping training sets. It is not uncertainty
from independent replications; calibration-mask and cohort sensitivity remain pending.

</details>

## 5. Response functions

These fitted associations are shown on the representative fold, with nearby
measured profiles for context. Shading is a pointwise 95% credible interval
for the mean, excluding response noise; it is not a response prediction interval.

### Observable mean m(x,c)

- **Slice:** salinity 34.20; vary pressure within each \(c\) level.
- **Comparison:** EIV O0/O20/O50 and original \((x,c)\) baselines; \(m\) integrates the fitted conditional \(u\) distribution.

```{r category-mean-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) print(surfaces$plots$m_comparison) else cat("Category-mean displays are pending complete final fits.\n")
```

### Calibrated response function f(x,u)

- **Slice:** salinity 34.25, pressure 650 dbar; vary \(u\) over the central range of nearby reference profiles.
- **Interpretation:** O20/O50 provide calibrated coordinates; nearby observations do not guarantee dense joint support. This differs from the \(x\) slice used for \(m\).

```{r continuous-surface-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) print(surfaces$plots$f_with_observations) else cat("Continuous-response displays are pending calibrated final fits.\n")
```

**Point markers:** filled = training; hollow = test. Blue rings identify training
calibration shared by O20/O50; orange rings identify additional O50 calibration.
Masked \(u\) is positioned using offline references only. Nearby profiles have
varying \(x\) and noisy responses, so their distance from a mean band is not a
coverage diagnostic. These plots do not establish true-surface recovery.

## 6. Training-input imputation

The posterior \(p(u_i\mid D)\) uses training \(y_i\). Evaluation compares O20/O50
on the same `r inputs$design$n_common_hidden` hidden training profiles per fold; it does not assess prospective
\(u\) prediction without \(y\). O0 is shown on its unanchored working coordinate.

```{r imputation-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=13.2, fig.height=6}
if(is.null(diagnostics)) cat("Imputation displays are pending complete final fits.\n") else {
  u_tables <- ocean_paper_u_tables(diagnostics$u$summary)
  cat(ocean_table_html(ocean_table_columns(u_tables$main,setdiff(names(u_tables$main),"MAE")),
    "Response-informed training oxygen imputation",u_tables$note),"\n\n")
  print(diagnostics$plots$u_main)
}
```

Hollow points are observed calibration inputs; solid points and intervals summarize
hidden-input posteriors. Overall bias can conceal opposing class biases, and
narrower intervals alone do not establish better calibration.

### Marginal distribution of hidden training inputs

- **Solid curve:** pool the posterior draws of the same `r inputs$design$n_common_hidden` hidden profiles, with equal weight per profile.
- **Gray histogram:** the actual measured \(u\) values of those `r inputs$design$n_common_hidden` profiles, withheld from fitting; bar area represents empirical frequency. Rug marks individual measurements.
- **O0:** posterior draws remain in model units. There is no training calibration to identify a physical oxygen scale, so raw measured \(u\) cannot be overlaid. O20/O50 use physical units and identical reference histograms.

```{r overall-input-distribution, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5}
u_distributions <- ocean_u_distribution_report(output_dir,inputs,params$representative_fold)
if(!is.null(u_distributions))print(u_distributions$pooled_plot)
```

Compare location, spread and tails with the measured distribution. This marginal
check includes between-profile variation; individual interval calibration remains
assessed by the preceding imputation plot and coverage summaries.

### Class-specific imputation calibration

The model learns cutpoints; its extreme categories are unbounded. Individual-U
intervals can therefore exceed the constructed \(c\) intervals or cohort bounds.
Detailed counts are provided below without clipping intervals.

```{r support-and-class-calibration, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(diagnostics)) {
  d <- ocean_paper_u_tables(diagnostics$u$summary)$class
  cat(ocean_table_html(ocean_table_columns(d,setdiff(names(d),"MAE")),"Training-U imputation by c",
    "Entries are five-fold means (sample SDs) on common-hidden training rows. Bias, RMSE and width use micromol/kg. Aggregate bias can conceal opposing class biases."))
  z <- diagnostics$u$summary
  cov <- z[z$metric=="Coverage95" & grepl("^class[0-9]+$",z$group),]
  lowest <- do.call(rbind,lapply(split(cov,cov$cell),function(a)a[which.min(a$mean),,drop=FALSE]))
  if(nrow(lowest)) {
    text <- sprintf("%s: c=%s, %.1f%%",lowest$cell,sub("class","",lowest$group),100*lowest$mean)
    cat(paste0("\n\nLowest class-specific mean coverage: ",paste(text,collapse="; "),". ",
      if(any(lowest$mean<.95))"At least one class falls below the nominal 95%; overall bias and response coverage do not establish individual-input calibration." else
      "All displayed class-specific mean coverage estimates meet or exceed 95%; interval widths remain relevant.","\n\n"))
  }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Supplementary: class-specific imputed-input distributions</summary>

- **Solid curve:** equally weighted mixture of the individual \(u_i\) posteriors within each \(c\).
- **Gray histogram / rug:** empirical distribution / individual measured values for the same `r inputs$design$n_common_hidden/4` hidden profiles per class. These values are withheld from fitting.
- **Columns:** O0/O20/O50 on the same `r inputs$design$n_common_hidden` common-hidden profiles. O0 remains in model units; O20/O50 share histogram bins, physical axes and posterior smoothing within each class.
- **Reading:** compare location, spread and tails with references. Marginal spread includes differences between individuals; it cannot establish individual posterior contraction or coverage. Increasing calibration need not narrow every distribution.

```{r input-distributions, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=11}
if(!is.null(u_distributions))print(u_distributions$plot)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Supplementary: individual-input interval support</summary>

An interval is counted when either endpoint lies outside the constructed
\(c\) interval. This checks support compatibility, not reference-value coverage
or posterior probability outside the interval. Learned model cutpoints differ
from the construction boundaries; the extreme model categories have unbounded
endpoints and do not enforce \(0<u<180\).

```{r input-support-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(saved_review)) {
  d <- saved_review$support
  names(d)<-c("Calibration","c","Fold-row N","Unique profiles","Interval outside c (N)",
    "Lower < 0 (N)","Upper > 180 (N)","Mean < 0 (N)")
  d$Calibration <- paste0(sub("O","",d$Calibration),"%")
  cat(ocean_table_html(d,"Individual-U interval support checks",
    "Counts include repeated training appearances across folds. These endpoint-exceedance counts are not posterior tail probabilities. Intervals are not clipped."))
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Supplementary: training-input imputation across folds</summary>

```{r all-fold-imputation, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile!="quick" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, fig.width=13.2, fig.height=14}
if(!is.null(diagnostics)) print(diagnostics$plots$u_all_folds)
```

</details>

## 7. Reproducibility and references

- **Execution:** task seeds are independent of assignment/order; receipts validate reuse and merging. Logs are under `logs/<run_id>/` in new flat roots (legacy `jobs/<run_id>/` remains supported).
- **Prediction evidence:** `prediction_report/cc_revision/` contains current recorded-input/CC/EIV scores and EIV-only matched-input evidence. Each CC task records the precise training/test IDs, transforms, controls, seed and native status.
- **Input distributions:** `diagnostics/u_distributions/` records common-hidden profile references and plotted density curves; posterior states are thinned deterministically for visualization only.
- **Posterior review:** `diagnostics/refinement/` contains input-support checks, diagnostic exceptions and selected full-chain MCSE.
- **Pending experiments:** PI-GP, additional calibration masks and formal UC-GP optimization are not included in these results.

The HTML embeds its figures. Environment requirements and provenance are in
`README_ocean.md`.

Data: GLODAPv2.2023, DOI **10.25921/zyrq-ht66**. Product reference:
Lauvset et al. (2024), *Earth System Science Data* 16, 2047–2072,
DOI **10.5194/essd-16-2047-2024**.
